traits.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon), western bracken: stipes erect, stout, 15 to 100 cm; blades triangular to triangular-ovate, 25 to 100 cm, nearly ternately decompound, usually three times pinnate below.

traits.ternate_blade.note: Abrams's flora (vol. 1, 1923; ferns by Maxon), western bracken: blades "nearly ternately decompound", so usually rather than always ternate.

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS, Crane (1990), western brackenfern: frost kills the fronds, so in cold climates they die each winter and new ones come up in spring; in mild places a frond may live two or three years.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a tall fern spreading by deep rhizomes into dense stands of single, broad, triangular fronds held flat on stiff stalks. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.5 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: light green fronds, brown by late summer.
